title: Completed and rational tensor-Hom transpose bijection
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient datum of [def-fix-six-functor-datum], a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $X$, and a finite coefficient field $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with $R=\mathcal O_E$. Use the derived-complete bounded constructible integral category $D^b_c(X,R)$ of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], its completed coefficient sheaf $\widehat R_X$, and the tensor, internal Hom and evaluation operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Let $P,L,Q\in D^b_c(X,R)$ and assume $H(P,Q)=R\mathcal Hom_{\widehat R_X}(P,Q)$ belongs to $D^b_c(X,R)$. Write $e_{P,Q}:P\widehat\otimes_R^L H(P,Q)\to Q$ for evaluation. Then the map
$$\operatorname{Hom}(L,H(P,Q))\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(P\widehat\otimes_R^L L,Q),\qquad \varphi\longmapsto e_{P,Q}\circ(1_P\widehat\otimes_R^L\varphi)$$
is an $R$-linear bijection, natural in all three variables on the indicated domains and compatible with the signed tensor symmetry. In the raw rationalization $D^b_c(X,E)$ of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], for the images of these objects and operations the same evaluation formula gives a natural $E$-linear bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}(L,R\mathcal Hom_E(P,Q))\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}(P\otimes_E^L L,Q).$$
This rational bijection applies to arbitrary morphisms in the rationalized Hom groups, and retains the naturality and symmetry compatibility.

proof.text: On the ringed pro-etale site with coefficient sheaf $\widehat R_X$, put $H=R\mathcal Hom_{\widehat R_X}$. The global-sections identification $H^0(R\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{proet}},R\mathcal Hom(A,B)))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(A,B)$ and the natural currying isomorphism $H(L,H(P,Q))\cong H(L\otimes^L P,Q)$ give a natural chain $\operatorname{Hom}(L,H(P,Q))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(L\otimes^L P,Q)$. The canonical signed symmetry of the derived tensor changes the target to $\operatorname{Hom}(P\otimes^L L,Q)$. By the closed tensor-Hom model, the resulting bijection is the transpose of the evaluation counit, hence sends $\varphi$ to $e_{P,Q}\circ(1_P\otimes^L\varphi)$.

source.place: Tags 08JA and 08J9; internal-Hom currying and global derived Hom

proof.text:
Put $\mathcal O=\widehat R_X$ and $B_n=(R/\varpi^n)_X$. Choose flat-term K-flat representatives $A\to P$ and $B\to L$ as in [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. The actual tensor identifications
$$ (A\otimes_{\mathcal O}B)\otimes_{\mathcal O}B_n
 \cong (A\otimes_{\mathcal O}B_n)\otimes_{B_n}(B\otimes_{\mathcal O}B_n) $$
commute with the quotient transitions: both send $(a\otimes b)\otimes\bar r$ to $(a\otimes\bar r)\otimes(b\otimes1)$ and apply the same quotient to $\bar r$. The canonical K-flat total-tensor model in [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model] therefore identifies the completed tensor construction with $\widehat T=R\lim_n\operatorname{Res}_n(T\otimes^L_{\mathcal O}B_n)$, for $T=P\otimes^L_{\mathcal O}L$, respecting its unit $\eta_T:T\to\widehat T$. The constant/completed-coefficient comparison identifies this quotient-tower completion, with its unit, with Koszul completion. The coefficient ring is the Noetherian DVR $R$ and the ideal is the principal ideal $(\varpi)$, so this comparison applies. The reflector then gives a natural bijection $\eta_T^*:\operatorname{Hom}(\widehat T,Q)\to\operatorname{Hom}(T,Q)$. The definition of derived completeness puts $Q$ isomorphically in this completion subcategory, so the reflector applies; no choice of a lift in an abstract Roos triangle is used to define $\eta_T$. Compose the bijection of Step 1 with $(\eta_T^*)^{-1}$. For $H=H(P,Q)$, completed evaluation is the unique extension of ambient evaluation along $\eta_{P\otimes^L H}$; the coefficient-system evaluation calculus preserves that evaluation comparison. Naturality of the completion unit gives
$$ (1_P\widehat\otimes\varphi)\eta_T=\eta_{P\otimes^L H}(1_P\otimes\varphi). $$
Thus $e_{P,Q}(1_P\widehat\otimes\varphi)$ restricts along $\eta_T$ to the ambient transpose of $\varphi$. Uniqueness in the reflector bijection proves that the resulting map is exactly the displayed completed evaluation transpose.

proof.text: The ambient currying and its global-sections identification are natural in the three inputs, as are the completion unit and the evaluation comparisons cited in Steps 1--2. Uniqueness of extension through that unit transports these naturality equations to completed tensors. All these maps are $R$-linear. To check the symmetry convention, use the fixed K-flat tensor and Hom representative models. If $p$ has degree $a$ and $l$ degree $b$, the degree-zero map $\varphi$ sends $l$ to a Hom element of degree $b$. Currying on $L\otimes P$ sends $l\otimes p$ to $\varphi(l)(p)$. Precomposition with the signed symmetry on $P\otimes L$ sends $p\otimes l$ to $(-1)^{ab}\varphi(l)(p)$. This is also evaluation on $P\otimes H(P,Q)$: it is ordinary evaluation on $H(P,Q)\otimes P$ preceded by its signed symmetry. Both transposition constructions therefore have the identical sign. The calculation respects quotient maps and localization of the representative complexes; uniqueness through completion proves the same equality for the completed tensors.

proof.text: In the raw rationalization, the objects are unchanged and each Hom group is $\operatorname{Hom}_{D^b_c(X,R)}(-,-)\otimes_R E$. The integral tensor and internal-Hom maps, including evaluation, extend $E$-linearly by the rational operation definitions. Tensoring the integral natural $R$-linear bijection with the field $E$ therefore gives an $E$-linear bijection on the full rationalized Hom groups, for arbitrary rational morphisms; the naturality and signed-symmetry equations persist after scalar extension.
